s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painless nodules with ulceration and hemorrhagic crusts on the fingers, accompanied by discomfort and pain along the arm and forearm
salient_findings: Vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the arm and forearm
key_facts: 30-year-old male
Dairy farm worker
Multiple painless nodules on fingers of both hands
Nodules appeared 1 month prior to presentation
Vesicles developed 7-10 days after initial nodules
Hemorrhagic crusts formed after vesicles ruptured
Discomfort and pain along medial aspect of right arm and forearm
Denies trauma or insect bites
Cow had similar lesions on its teats
3-4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema on proximal phalanges of both hands
Mild tenderness and increased warmth along medial right arm and forearm

shortlist.label: Erysipeloid
shortlist.why_kept: Occupational exposure to animals and clinical presentation of painless nodules with ulceration and hemorrhagic crusts

shortlist.label: Orf virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar lesions on the cow's teats and the patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker

shortlist.label: Milker's nodule
shortlist.why_kept: Painless nodules on the fingers and occupational exposure to cows

shortlist.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and occupational exposure to animals

shortlist.label: Pseudocowpox
shortlist.why_kept: Similar lesions on the cow's teats and the patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker

raw.rationale: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on the cow's teats, along with the characteristic clinical presentation of multiple painless nodules on the fingers that developed into vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts, are consistent with Milker's nodule, a paravaccinia virus infection that is commonly seen in individuals who handle infected cows.

rejected.label: Erysipeloid
rejected.why: While erysipeloid can cause similar lesions, it is typically associated with more systemic symptoms and a history of handling infected animals, particularly pigs, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Orf virus infection
rejected.why: Orf virus infection typically presents with a single lesion, often on the hand or finger, and is associated with handling infected sheep or goats, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
rejected.why: This is another term for Milker's nodule, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.

rejected.label: Pseudocowpox
rejected.why: Pseudocowpox is another term for Milker's nodule or paravaccinia virus infection, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.
